question: Which of the following elements of the periodic table has atomic number 1?
solution:
The correct answer is __Hydrogen.__​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hydrogen has atomic number 1 and is placed in group 1 along with alkali metals.
 
• It is the first element in the periodic table.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hydrogen was discovered by Henry Cavendish.
 
• Hydrogen gas is called the fuel of the future.
 
• The most abundant element in the universe is Hydrogen.
 
• The most abundant element on earth's crust is Oxygen.
 
• Hydrogen is the 'lightest element' in the periodic table.
 
• Lithium is the 'lightest metal' in the periodic table.
